assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks transformed attainable measurement precision and made coherent atomic control a practical route to new fundamental tests.
assessment.attribution: Katori represents magic-wavelength trapping, Ye the high-precision realization. Their complementary roles make a clear paired proposal.
assessment.maturity: The platform is mature, with independent implementations and clock comparisons.
uncertainties: The packet gives no explicit uncertainty budgets or historical priority evidence; a final assessment needs both.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry opened powerful measurements of gravity, inertia and fundamental constants, with applications extending beyond laboratory physics.
assessment.attribution: Bordé represents theoretical atom optics, Pritchard material-grating demonstration and Kasevich light-pulse realization.
assessment.maturity: The essential coherent splitting and precision-sensing capabilities have extensive reproducible history.
uncertainties: Architecture-specific priority and control of systematic errors are not described; the citation must fairly join distinct experimental routes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single-spin optical control made a solid-state quantum object into a useful sensor, with broad consequences for measurements on small spatial scales.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko represent detection and coherent control; Lukin sensing development. This is a plausible discovery-to-use configuration.
assessment.maturity: Core spin-control and magnetometry capabilities are established across laboratories.
uncertainties: The packet does not provide first-demonstration chronology, coherence benchmarks or application-specific sensitivity evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned foundational quantum effects into a new operational capability for secure communication.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard represent BB84, Ekert the entanglement-based route. Their conceptual contributions are complementary.
assessment.maturity: The protocols and physical demonstrations are mature; implemented security still depends on device models.
uncertainties: A final citation must distinguish ideal security proofs from experimentally certified security. The packet lacks a complete contribution history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new laser architecture created useful coherent sources for molecular spectroscopy through quantum-engineered electronic levels.
assessment.attribution: Faist and Capasso represent the laser invention and realization, Cho the enabling epitaxial structures.
assessment.maturity: Laser operation and spectroscopic usefulness are established and reproduced.
uncertainties: The precise division of invention, growth and device-design credit is not documented in the packet.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Controllable lattice gases made many-body quantum models measurable, changing experiments on strongly interacting systems.
assessment.attribution: Zoller represents theoretical model engineering; Bloch and Greiner the defining experimental realization and imaging.
assessment.maturity: The core Hubbard-model realization and Mott-transition results are mature and reproducible.
uncertainties: Cirac is also credited. A full historical assessment must distinguish initial proposal and experiment from later theoretical extensions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Photonic band gaps opened a structural way to control propagation and emission, with lasting impact on optical confinement and devices.
assessment.attribution: Yablonovitch and John represent original principles; Joannopoulos important theoretical-design development. The third position is provisional.
assessment.maturity: The principle and useful structures have a long record of independent realization.
uncertainties: The packet does not fix whether the prize honors conceptual discovery or later engineering; attribution may differ between those scopes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Closed optical cycling and molecular trapping opened a difficult new class of coherent systems to controlled laboratory study and precision sensing.
assessment.attribution: DeMille and Doyle represent foundational molecular laser-cooling work; Tarbutt further cooling and trapping development. The configuration is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Direct cooling and trapping are demonstrated capabilities, with sustained independent development.
uncertainties: The packet lacks species-specific evidence, scattering-cycle budgets and exact priority history. Broad utility and performance across molecules should not be assumed.
